posts.title: Welcome to your portfolio
posts.content:
This whole site — tabs, blocks, cards, hero, blog — is one JSON document. What you are reading is the demo seed that ships with the repository, written to show off what the platform can do before you replace all of it with your own work.

What is actually in this portfolio

  • Home — the marketing pitch: a centered hero with a call-to-action that jumps to another tab, a scrolling feature marquee, a card grid, and this blog block.
  • Showcase — the same building blocks wearing their four art directions: default, cutie, editorial, and riso. Same data, four personalities.
  • Guide — real instructions for editing, publishing, and replacing this demo.
  • Playground — the custom HTML block doing things the other blocks can't: custom CSS and a video embed.

Under the hood you are looking at: five skin options with token-driven motion, per-block design pickers, a reusable card library (one edit propagates everywhere), drag-and-drop ordering, undo/redo, a media vault, a full blog engine, and view scale control. The Guide tab walks through all of it.

Know the limits

The platform is honest about what it is not (yet):

  • Mobile is untested — everything renders, but serious editing wants a desktop.
  • Last save wins — two devices editing the same hosted portfolio means no merge; the newest Save replaces everything.
  • Images do not migrate — export/import moves content, not image bytes; externally-hosted image URLs are the safe form.
  • Auth is a guardrail — the self-hosted password gate stops accidents, not attackers.

Make it yours

Open the editor, drag things around, change the words, and export the result. Nothing here is precious: the demo exists to be deleted.

  • Press Ctrl/Cmd + Shift + E (or visit with ?edit=true) to edit
  • Read the Guide tab for the full walkthrough
  • Check the Playground tab for the custom CSS and embed demos

posts.title: How to build a portfolio here
posts.content:
A practical recipe, from empty fork to published site — plus the fine print worth knowing before you start.

1. Get the code running

Fork the repository, run npm install and npm run dev, and open localhost:3000. That is the whole setup — the editor works with zero configuration.

2. Enter edit mode

Visit with ?edit=true or press Ctrl/Cmd + Shift + E. You get the block editor, the hidden Posts and Site tabs, and undo/redo history.

3. Fill in your content

Add a hero, an app grid, an entry list, a marquee. Give each block its own art direction — the four designs are siblings, so the same data renders four different ways. Reorder by dragging, duplicate cards from the library, set skins, accent color, font, and view scale in Site settings.

4. Publish (the fork path)

Press Export in the editor toolbar, open the downloaded JSON, and copy-paste its contents over content/portfolio.json in your repo. Commit any images you reference under public/images (uploads are gitignored), then git push. The rebuild is the publish — the site bakes the document at build time.

5. Or go hosted

Deploy with the Vercel checklist in the README (Firebase + Cloudflare KV + R2), sign up from the hub, onboard, and press Save — visitors get your work at /u/your-name immediately, no rebuilds. The export/import bridge moves an existing portfolio between the two worlds; just remember it carries content, not image bytes.

The fine print

  • Editing is desktop-first; mobile renders but is untested for real work.
  • Hosted saves are last-save-wins — one editor at a time is the safe assumption.
  • The self-hosted password gate is a guardrail, not security; hosted accounts use real Firebase auth.
  • If something breaks, open an issue on the repository — a lot of this is young and untested, and reports directly shape the roadmap.

blocks.content:
Three things to try right now

1. Press Ctrl/Cmd + Shift + E. Seriously, do it. This entire page just became editable — drag things, break things, there is an undo button.

2. Click the tabs up top. Showcase, Guide, Playground — same engine, four art directions, and a playground with custom CSS and a video embed.

3. Scroll down a little. The blog is right there — two stories about turning this demo into your portfolio. Go read them, then come back and press that button up top.
Every block picks its own art direction. This tab shows the same building blocks wearing all four — default, cutie, editorial, riso — because design is a per-block choice, not a site-wide one.

blocks.content:
First time here? Start exactly here.

This tab is the tour. Nothing you do can break the site — the demo resets from one file, and there is undo.

Step 1. Press Ctrl/Cmd + Shift + E right now. Poof — edit mode. Panels appeared, the page grew little handles.

Step 2. Find the + Entry List button at the bottom of the side panel and press it. You just added a block. Change its words. Drag it by the ⠿ handle.

Step 3. Feel the power? Press Ctrl/Cmd + Z a few times and watch it un-happen. That is undo. Welcome to the rest of the tour below.

Make it yours

Everything below happens in the browser — no code, no restart.

  • Edit mode: visit with ?edit=true or press Ctrl/Cmd + Shift + E
  • Per-block design: every block has a design picker — default, cutie, editorial, riso
  • Entry lists: pick a preset for the form labels and 1–3 columns for the layout
  • Site settings: skins, accent color, global font, and view scale live in the hidden Site tab
  • Ordering: drag and drop blocks, cards, tabs, and entry rows — keyboard reordering works too
  • History: Ctrl/Cmd + Z and Ctrl/Cmd + Shift + Z undo and redo everything
  • Media vault: upload images or paste https URLs, then reference them anywhere

Publish it

Two products share this codebase, and the JSON document is the bridge between them.

  • Product B (fork, zero-config): export the JSON and replace content/portfolio.json, then git push — a rebuild publishes it
  • Product A (hosted): sign in, edit, and press Save in the toolbar — the server sanitizes and persists the document
  • Bridge: the export/import endpoints move a portfolio between the two; only image URLs travel, so externally hosted pictures migrate cleanly

Or skip the code entirely — go hosted

Everything you are looking at can run as a hosted service: sign up, pick a design, and your portfolio is live at /u/your-name the moment you press Save. No repository, no rebuilds, no git — edits go straight to the cloud and visitors see them instantly.

  • Live in minutes: deploy once with the README checklist, then the dashboard is your home — create, edit, publish, and browse everyone else's public portfolios in the showcase.
  • Onboarding builds it for you: pick an art direction, type your name, and a real starter portfolio is generated before you ever see the editor.
  • Real accounts: email or Google sign-in, your document stored server-side, images on cloud storage — your work follows you to any device.
  • Bring this demo with you: the export/import bridge moves portfolios between the fork and the hosted product in both directions.

The fork is for tinkerers; hosted is for everyone else. Same editor, same designs, same document — pick the workflow that fits.

Replace the demo

This entire portfolio is one JSON document — edit it, export it, wipe it. The README documents the demo seed, the hosted setup, and the deploy checklist on GitHub.
